newsitem.title: USA: Pfizer plans 4 new drug filings through 97.
newsitem.headline: Pfizer plans 4 new drug filings through 97.

text.p: Pfizer Inc said on Monday it expects to seek U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for four new drugs, including treatments for irregular heartbeats and male impotence, by the end of 1997.
Pharmaceutical industry analysts said the new drugs could be major additions to the company's sales but were cautious ahead of seeing final details on how safe and effective they are.

Next year "should lay the groundwork for the growth of our pharmaceutical business well into the next century," John Niblack, Pfizer's executive vice president for research and development, told a meeting with analysts and investors.
Pfizer's Viagra could be the first oral drug for treating male impotence, Pfizer executives said.

Current approved drugs include Pharmacia & Upjohn's Caverject, which involes an injection directly into the penis, and Vivus Inc's MUSE system, which uses a single-dose applicator of a drug that increases blood flow.
If it works well, Viagra could have annual sales of $500 million, said Montgomery Securities' John Borzilleri. "There's big potential if the efficacy is real good," he said.
Pfizer plans to file Viagra in 1997's fourth quarter, company executives said.
The company said it also plans to file its dofedtilide drug for treating heart arrhythmias in 1997's fourth quarter.

Analysts, however, were wary about gauging the drug's sales potential noting several other drug companies have had to drop attempts to develop arrhythmia drugs because of dangerous, sometimes deadly, side effects.
But noting that Pfizer has advanced in late-stage clincial trials with dofedtilide, Cowen and Co's Ian Sanderson said, "They must have seen some pretty good results to date."
Pfizer executives said they expected to file trovafloxicin, a quinolone antibiotic, with the FDA in December for treating 12 types of infections.
Analysts said the drug could have an advantage over other potent antibiotics because it will be available in pill form, in addition to an intravenous formulation.
Pfizer also plans to file its anti-psychotic drug ziprasidone in 1997's second quarter.
The drug is one of a new line of anti-schizophrenia treatments that includes Johnson and Johnson 's Risperdal and Eli Lilly and Co's Zyprexa, both of which are already on the market.

Pfizer executives said company partner Eisai Co Ltd expects to have the Alzheimer's disease treatment Aricept receive final FDA approval by the end of 1996. The FDA last month issued a letter saying the drug was approvable.

They also said they expected the cholesterol-lowering drug atorvastatin, which Pfizer is co-promoting the U.S. with Warner-Lambert Co, to be approved and launched in 1997. The drug was filed with the FDA in June.
In addition to the new drugs, Pfizer executives said they expect to file through 1997 for four add-on uses for company drugs already on the market.
They said that in 1996 17 new drug candidates will be added to the company's early development pipeline.
Pfizer's shares were off 3/4 at 80 in Friday afternoon trade.
--New York Newsdesk, 212-859-1733
